title_en: Don't Worry, CD Projekt's Partnership With Sony Doesn't Mean The Witcher 4 and Its Other Games Are Going PlayStation Exclusive
summary_en: CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has reassured fans that The Witcher 4 remains a multiplatform game despite its PlayStation marketing deal with Sony.
body_en:
CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has reassured fans that The Witcher 4 remains a multiplatform game despite its PlayStation marketing deal with Sony.
Announced yesterday as part of CD Projekt’s latest financial results , the partnership with Sony Interactive Entertainment also covers its games on PlayStation and PlayStation Plus. CD Projekt said the deal “will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.”
While the terms of the deal remain undisclosed, it is expected that The Witcher 4 marketing will feature PS5 prominently, perhaps even exclusively, as GTA 6’s marketing has done with the “Plays Best on PS5” tagline.
In a follow-up post on social media , Nowakowski insisted The Witcher 4, which is slated for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X and S, remains a multiplatform release, as do all the games CD Projekt has in the works. That presumably means no exclusivity deal for Cyberpunk 2, not that anyone suspected one might be put in place.
“We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation! And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform,” Nowakowski said.
Already there is concern around The Witcher 4’s PlayStation marketing deal, following the debate around GTA 6’s “Plays Best on PS5” tagline. As we’ve reported, the Xbox Series X version of Rockstar’s epic has better performance than the PS5 version , which has caused some to say they feel misled.
The Witcher 4 isn’t due out until 2028 so there’s a long time to go before we see the result of CD Projekt’s effort, but marketing is expected to ramp up significantly in the coming months. Excitement is building, and this week CD Projekt said it expects the leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 to be comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6 .
As of October 31, 2026, CD Projekt had 513 staff working on The Witcher 4, which is actually down slightly on the previous number reported three months earlier. The number of people working on Cyberpunk 2, however, has ramped up, from 184 to 199.
CD Projekt has a huge amount going on right now. The Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, launches next year, followed by The Witcher 4 in 2028. CD Projekt has an ambitious plan to release further The Witcher sequels hot on the heels of The Witcher 4 as part of a new trilogy of games. Then there’s Cyberpunk 2 to squeeze in there at some point, The Witcher remake, Project Hadar, and Project Sirius.
